records.name: Sikkim
records.summary:
No Sikkim-specific trans statute, enforcement series or incident pattern is on file; the state sits under the national framework, which narrowed sharply in March 2026: parliament removed the self-identification right affirmed by the 2014 Supreme Court ruling, restricted recognition to intersex variations and traditional community identities certified by medical boards, and made board certification mandatory for gender-affirming surgery. A court-appointed advisory panel asked the government to withdraw the bill, prominent trans activists warned of mass exclusion, protests followed the vote, and presidential assent is pending.

The framework's enforcement texture nationally includes transit-space 'gender checks': an August 2024 case at a northern railway station, in which a trans traveller alleged a rail-police constable groped her while checking her gender — police denied it and filed a counter-complaint — evidences a policing habit of treating trans appearance as suspicion in federally-policed transit spaces rather than in this state specifically.

records.name: Odisha
records.summary:
No Odisha-specific trans statute, welfare-board finding or incident series is on file; the state sits under the national framework, which narrowed sharply in March 2026: parliament removed the self-identification right affirmed by the 2014 Supreme Court ruling, restricted recognition to intersex variations and board-certified traditional identities, and made medical-board certification mandatory for gender-affirming surgery, drawing warnings of exclusion from activists, a withdrawal request from a court-appointed advisory panel, and protests after the vote, with presidential assent pending.

Nationally, the recognition-to-enforcement gap for trans people includes transit-space 'gender checks' — an August 2024 railway-policing allegation from another state (denied by police with a counter-complaint) is the kind of federally-policed practice that applies in Odisha's stations and transit corridors without being an Odisha pattern.

records.name: Ladākh
records.summary: Reconstituted in 2019 from the former state of Jammu and Kashmir into a union territory without its own legislature, so trans-related policy depends on the central government (an RTI survey counts Ladakh among the 19 states/UTs with no transgender welfare body). Beyond this administrative framework the country dossier found no region-specific trans law, enforcement series or incident pattern material enough to score separately (±0.02); assessed at the national score.
